chunks: Among them is Duraid ibn al-Samah al-Jashami, who lived for two hundred years and witnessed the era of Islam but did not accept it. He was one of the commanders of the polytheists on the day of Hunain and was at their forefront. He attended the war of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and was killed on that day.

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ الْإِسْلَامَ: Witnessed/encountered Islam, meaning he lived during its early period
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِ: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.الْجَشَمِيُّ: Al-Jashami, referring to the Jasham tribe
key_terms.دُرَيْدُ بْنُ الصَّمَةِ: Duraid ibn al-Samah, a specific historical figure
key_terms.مِائَتَيْ سَنَةٍ: Two hundred years, indicating his long lifespan
key_terms.يَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ: The day of Hunain, a specific historical battle

ai.seo_question: Who was Duraid ibn al-Samah and what was his role in the Battle of Hunain?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the phenomenon of *Tawallud* (longevity) among pre-Islamic Arabs, using Duraid ibn al-Samah as a prime example of a polytheist leader who lived through the transition to Islam yet remained steadfast in his disbelief. His presence at the Battle of Hunain highlights the continuity of tribal leadership structures even as the Islamic community consolidated power, serving as a historical counterpoint to the eventual triumph of the believers.
